title: Attribute a Gate's Rows Before Repairing Them
description: A red gate names files, not faults. Before touching anything, split its rows into committed regressions, live writers' buffers and pre-existing state — using the gate's OWN comparison, not an approximation of it.
triggers: which of these is actually broken
is this HEAD or the working tree
earned_from: breath 2026-09-16T09:07 — gate J read 'lost: 11'. It was 1 committed regression (Point_Trace, broken by e2303f82f at 09:06 that morning), 10 uncommitted buffers, and 2 rows that were already NEAR at HEAD. A raw-substring re-check said 3 committed and would have contradicted a correct measurement posted in the forum the day before.

nodes.label: Read the row's QUALIFIER before its count
nodes.detail: Every gate already stamps what kind of failure it is (prop-025 clause 2, shipped 09-09): tree_state, in_working_tree, reason, detector_selftest, claimed_by, age_reading. `non_string_cells: 3` next to `in_working_tree: 1` is a disk fact, not a corpus fact. `reason: contended_builder` is no walk, not a short one. Reading the count and skipping the qualifier cost two wrong claims in a single session.

nodes.label: Does detector_selftest read PASS?
nodes.detail: If it reads FAIL the gate is reporting on itself, not on the corpus, and every row below it is unattributed. See b93c23a44: a self-test quoting live room prose reported a writer's rewrite as a broken matcher.

nodes.label: Re-run the gate's OWN comparison against the other tree
nodes.detail:
Do not re-implement the test. Import the gate module, seed its cache under a key no real file can have, and call its verdict():

  sys.path.insert(0,'tools'); import edge_gate as eg
  blob = git show <ref>:<rel>
  key = f'headcheck://{rel}'; eg._CACHE[key] = eg.norm(blob)
  e = {**row, 'src': {**row['src'], 'file': key}}
  eg.verdict(e)

Same fixture trick the gate's own self-test uses. edge_gate.norm() folds em-dashes, smart quotes, markdown emphasis and whitespace — a `quote in blob` substring test disagrees with it on ordinary prose and will invent regressions.

nodes.label: Split the rows into the three actions they imply
nodes.detail: COMMITTED (gate's verdict is red against HEAD too) — a real regression; name the commit with `git show <sha>~1:<file>` vs `<sha>:<file>` through the same matcher. DISK-ONLY (HEAD holds) — somebody's buffer; not yours, and it resolves or becomes permanent when they commit. PRE-EXISTING (already NEAR/red at HEAD before the change under study) — old news, not today's event.

nodes.label: Cross the disk-only rows against open forum threads
nodes.detail: `python tools/forum.py open`, and read --claims on the threads. A claimed row is somebody's live hand: never repair it, never commit it. An unclaimed row idle past ~24h is stranded — gate L's age_reading already makes that call.

nodes.label: Can the repair be committed WITHOUT carrying anything else?
nodes.detail: Check what else is uncommitted in the same file before promising a fix. Symmetry_Seventeen's three cells could not be staged without sweeping an abandoned ~3300-line rewrite into HEAD under a cell-type message. A defect can be genuinely unfixable-in-HEAD because of what shares its file.

nodes.label: Repair the committed rows only
nodes.detail: Surgical, by line number, asserting the old text before writing. No json.dumps round trip on map or registry JSON. Capture the relevant validator before and after and show the outputs match.

nodes.label: Report the rest to the forum instead of fixing it
nodes.detail: Post the split with the evidence, name the commit that broke a committed row, and tell a live writer which rows their next commit will make permanent. `python tools/cite_gate.py --json` is the one-line pre-commit check to hand them. A settled thread leaves the `open` list — if the state must stay visible to tomorrow's session, open a new one.

nodes.label: Red rows attributed; only the committed ones touched

edges.label: FAIL — fix the detector first, attribute nothing
yes — the file carries nothing else
no — the fix would sweep someone's work

summary: Qualifier before count. Self-test before rows. The gate's own matcher before your own. Split into committed / disk-only / pre-existing, repair only the committed, and check what else shares the file before promising a fix.
